analysis:
Examined both workflow revisions, added changelog, build documentation and test-documentation patch, including metadata. No independently supported security regression in this scope. Provider transport, plaintext custody, attestation, serving grants, cache, billing ledger and privileged-helper controls are not changed; TB-002/TB-011 and related threat assumptions are not visibly invalidated.
.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml now restricts paid review to pull_request_target (head 68–69), removes manual PR resolution and dispatch-based Bedrock eligibility, and retains default-branch scanner checkout without persisted credentials (76–83), pinned actions/dependencies, explicit fork opt-in (64), and conditional clearance evaluation (168–174). It increases job duration to 60 minutes (55), supplies a 3000-second scanner deadline (131), and replaces the configurable fixed Bedrock call cap with workload policy and a 100-call ceiling (135–136). These enlarge bounded resource exposure but do not alone establish uncontrolled spending or clearance bypass.
Integration must verify .github/scripts/threat-model-review.py and its budget/client/gate dependencies consume these settings, enforce aggregate paid-call admission and spending limits, reject paid job reruns before calls, preserve findings on timeout, and deny incomplete/stale clearance. The workflow itself has no rerun guard; this is an unverified script contract, not evidence of a missing PR-wide control. Changelog lines 8–10, docs/developer/build.md:258–261 and docs/developer/test.md:729–735 claim those properties, but documentation is not implementation proof. Confirm the relative scanner deadline leaves reporting time after setup and that workload/repair/integration calls share the ceiling. Remaining material uncertainty concerns these changed CI contracts, not unrelated unchanged provider implementations.
